note: Single source for command boundaries. Rendered into Claude Code permission rules, Codex execpolicy rules, and OpenCode permission patterns. Edit this file, then run scripts/render.ps1.

decisions.allow: Runs without a prompt. Reserved for commands that cannot change state.
decisions.confirm: Prompts every time. Survives bypassPermissions in Claude Code.
decisions.forbid: Blocked. Survives bypassPermissions in Claude Code.

rules.why: Inspection changes nothing, so approving it only costs attention.
Recovering a force-pushed branch or a hard reset is manual and error prone. Make a focused reversible change instead.
rules.why_extra_rules: A prefix rule only matches when the flag is the third word. 'git push origin main --force' has it fifth, so the prefix rules above miss it. Claude Code and OpenCode both express a wildcard mid-pattern and close the gap. Codex prefix_rule cannot, so the Codex guarantee stays narrower. See docs/PROVIDERS.md.

rules.why: These throw away uncommitted work with no undo. Inspect and revert exact files instead.
Deleting a remote repository or release is never an incidental development action. Do it by hand after verifying the exact target.
A commit is the user's record of the work. Draft the message. Do not run git commit.
Pushing, publishing, and messaging are visible to other people the moment they run, and approval for one does not carry to the next.
Installing packages runs third-party install scripts and rewrites lockfiles that the rest of the project depends on.
Reading a credential into the transcript exposes it to the model provider and to anyone the transcript is later shared with.
rules.why_read_paths: A file-read boundary, not a command boundary. Claude Code renders these as Read() rules and OpenCode as permission.read entries. Codex has no file-read matcher, so it gets nothing from this rule, which is why its commands array is empty.
